crime: A week before leaving {WITCH_NAME} at her aunt's door, her mother taught her to plait her own hair: "Now you won't need me." She learned that people who teach you to manage without them are leaving.

One girl told {WITCH_NAME} her whole day in her head, from any room, and {WITCH_NAME} answered each silent word aloud. No other girl talked to {WITCH_NAME} like that. Each evening the girl used up the last of the hot water singing at the top of her voice, alone in the soundproof shower room.

At dinner in the dining hall, she said aloud, "Practise talking to the others out loud. You need more voices than mine." Under the words, {WITCH_NAME} heard her silent voice: "Then I can have my head to myself."

At nine, {WITCH_NAME} followed her into the shower room and shut the door behind them. As the girl sat on the bench drying her hair, {WITCH_NAME} twisted the towel round her throat from behind until she was still.

At twenty to ten, {WITCH_NAME} stopped a prisoner's hand on the shut door. The girls always asked her who was behind a shut door, and she had never been wrong. "She's still in there, singing in her head. She wants it to herself till ten." Then she went back to the lounge with them and stayed.
At five to ten, a prisoner opened the door to fetch the girl before lockup and found her slumped on the bench, the towel twisted at her throat.

In the trial court, the prisoners placed the strangling after twenty to ten, while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them in the lounge. Then a prisoner pointed to that door: not one note of the girl's singing had ever come through it, and a silent voice carries no further than a spoken one. The prisoners saw it: {WITCH_NAME} had heard nobody in there; she had said it because she had left the girl dead before twenty to ten.
fields.epitaph: The girl wanted only her head to herself, and she already had one room even you could never hear into.
fields.epithet: A listener who hears goodbye before it is spoken
execution: The execution stand raises a tall comb hung with three ropes of black hair, and she is strapped upright beneath it, at the center of the hanging strands. The strands begin to plait round her from the shoulders down, each crossing drawn tight across her ribs. At her ankles the plait ties itself off. No hand touches it. Now you won't need me. The finished plait hangs from the comb, and nothing inside it stirs.

magic.name: Every Unspoken Word
magic.text: She hears the unspoken thoughts of the people around her as clearly as spoken voices.
